content:
The lowest-cost tested design meeting your winter-outage requirement is a geothermal doublet at about 3062 m, a 30 MW backup boiler, a 10 MW electric screw chiller with dry cooler, associated-gas CHP and operating controls [R0193].

Its cost is 47.29 EUR/MWh, including the total carbon valuation of 180 EUR/t. Capital cost is 24.29 million EUR and annual emissions are 11,670 tonnes CO2 [R0193].

It meets heating and cooling demand throughout all 365 days, including a common 35-day geothermal shutdown covering the coldest day. Every hard rule passes. GEMINI’s native Solver also agrees on the checked operating day [R0193].

The search covered doublet counts, depths, heating upgrades, cooling technologies and CHP in screening grids of 48 configurations, followed by controls, sizing and storage refinements. Measured-weather free cooling and aquifer cold storage were tested but cost more [R0188, R0189]. Seasonal pit storage offers lower emissions at 48.67 EUR/MWh [R0192].

Key assumptions are the default energy prices and cost curves, heating/cooling returns of 40/26 degC, and Amsterdam Schiphol measured weather. Lower permeability also remained feasible, with higher cost [R0207].

Recommended: [R0193]
